_about: English glossary for the Learnings Coach (Ruling P3-21: translations land in Phase 4). do_not_translate marks names, codes and acronyms to keep as written in every language.

terms.definition: Eyekyam's human-in-the-loop, AI-assisted incident investigation service, built on HFACS. Its findings export is the only input the Learnings Coach accepts.

Human Factors Analysis and Classification System: a four-level framework (Unsafe Acts, Preconditions, Supervision, Organisational Influences) for classifying the human and organisational factors behind an event. See hfacs-levels.md.
The label the export's Analysis Statistics sheet uses for the same four HFACS-based levels. Use "HFACS-based" in audience-facing text.
One of the four HFACS levels, numbered 1 (Unsafe Acts) to 4 (Organisational Influences). The higher level enables the lower.
The HFACS category within a level, as written in the export's Subcategory column, for example "Failure to Correct Known Problem".
The factor code in a ProbeMatrix export, such as OIR 1.1: a prefix that fixes the level and sub-category, plus a factor number.
The letters before the space in a Nanocode (for example OIR), mapped one to one to a level and sub-category in hfacs-codes.json.
One evidence-linked factor identified by the analysis, with an ID such as FND-0012. Findings are the evidence beneath learnings, never the headline count.
The identifier of a finding (FND-…). Cite it on every sentence that rests on that finding.
One occurrence of a factor; the same Nanocode can appear as several findings, each an instance.
A document, record, statement or observation in the export's Evidence sheet, with an ID such as EVD-007. The only source of facts about the incident.
The identifier of an evidence item (EVD-…). Cite it next to the finding it supports.
The export field that quotes or locates the part of an evidence item that supports a finding. Quote facts from here, not from the AI justification.
The analysis's reasoning for a finding. Quote it only as "the analysis states", never as a fact.
The export's 1 to 5 score for how strongly a finding contributed; higher is stronger.
Supported by two or more independent evidence items.
A condition the organisation should change, stated once and supported by one or more findings. The unit the Learnings Coach counts.
A learning written down in a register, pack or briefing, not yet shown to have changed how work is done.
A learning that has changed how work is done, with the change checked to hold. See indicators-and-effectiveness.md.
A group of findings that share an owning entity (F), an organisational tier (T) and a relation (R). See ontology.md.
The function or part of the organisation that owns a learning (layer F in the taxonomy), such as Mechanical Maintenance.
The organisational level that learns (layer T): frontline, first-line supervision, function management, plant leadership, corporate and board.
How a role relates to a factor (layer R): actor, approver, owner, absent, norm_setter, learner or challenger.
The job or position named in a finding, used in place of any person's name.
A seam between two functions where findings or causal links are shared and responsibility can fall between them.
A connection from one factor to another written in the export's causal explanation or Causal Chain sheet. Arrows run from the enabling factor to the factor it enabled.
An earlier event, report or condition that pointed to the hazard before the incident.
A small or ambiguous early sign of a developing problem, easy to dismiss at the time.
An event that could have caused harm but did not, by chance or because a late barrier acted.
A source of potential harm, such as a flammable gas under pressure.
In a bow-tie, the moment control of the hazard is lost, such as a loss of containment.
In a bow-tie, a way the top event can come about.
In a bow-tie, an outcome that can follow the top event.
A condition that weakens a barrier, such as a detector out of service.
A diagram with threats and prevention barriers on the left of a top event, and mitigation barriers and outcomes on the right.
Anything that stands between a hazard and harm, by preventing a loss of control or limiting what follows it. See barriers-and-controls.md.
A barrier between a threat and the top event.
A barrier between the top event and an outcome, such as detection, isolation or fire protection.
How a barrier performed on the day: absent, degraded, defeated, worked partly or worked.
A measure that delivers or supports a barrier: a design feature, device, procedure, check or competence.
A control whose absence or failure would significantly raise the risk of a major event, even with other controls in place.
The order of control strength: elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, training, PPE.
A control that removes the hazard.
A control that replaces the hazard with a lesser one.
A control that designs the hazard away from people or acts on it automatically, including isolation, separation, interlocks and trips.
A control that changes how work is organised: procedures, checks, permits, plans, reviews, audits and sign-offs.
Personal protective equipment: the weakest tier, protecting only the individual wearing it.
A formal written system that authorises specific hazardous work, with its precautions, at a stated place and time.
A step in a job that must not be passed until a named role has checked and accepted the work so far.
The process for reviewing and approving a change to plant, process, procedure or organisation before it is made.
Physical isolation of energy sources with locks and tags so that equipment cannot be started while work is under way.
Separating equipment from its energy or process sources; physical isolation is an engineering control, the isolation procedure an administrative one.
A measure of barrier health or of the activities that keep it healthy, which changes before harm happens.
A measure of outcomes, such as releases or injuries, which confirms a trend after the fact.
The indicator value or pattern that starts a defined response by its owner.
Learning that corrects the work within the existing rules, goals and assumptions.
Learning that changes the rules, goals, assumptions or norms that let the condition arise.
An approach in which people are not blamed for actions that match their experience and training, while the organisation fixes the system conditions behind them.
In a report comparison, a learning that the comparator report also contains.
In a report comparison, a learning that the comparator report does not contain.
Another report on the same event, such as an official inquiry, compared with the ProbeMatrix learnings.
The table of learnings, one row per learning, with evidence, level, barrier, audiences and recommendations.
A structured JSON output for one audience, checked with check-pack and rendered to HTML and Markdown by the engine.
The folder the engine writes from one export (findings, evidence, clusters), under pmlc-runs/<date>-<site>-<event>/workspace.
The record that a named role has reviewed a pack or register; until then the output is a draft.
An output that no person has yet reviewed and signed off.
Something the analysis could not see or the export does not say, marked [GAP] rather than guessed.
A proposed change, with its barrier, control tier, evidence and leading indicator.
A shortfall in knowledge or skill where the way of working is defined, workable and done correctly by others in the role.
A condition in procedures, design, resources or supervision that training alone cannot fix.
